source: BK3 printed p.43 = book2-3-4.pdf PDF p.49; ERRATA ER-11 (prose), ER-12 (wire 2+/2H to 1G/2H); Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Speculative (Step 7): every expect is derived by hand from the corrected wiring and the p.43 rule (light 3 ON only when relay 1 AND relay 2 are ON), covering all four input combinations. Only both-pressed -> light 3 ON is printed (A/III-RELAYAND); light 3 with either relay OFF and the pushbutton-to-relay drive are unprinted (programs.json printedUnprinted). Topology: pushbutton n (nY on n+, nX on nC) drives relay n C-F through its indicator lamp (BK1 p.14: C-F drive lights the indicator); light 3 is the series chain 1+/1H-1G/2H-2G/3A, 3B/3- through the two normally open set-1 contacts. No contact feeds a coil, so there is no latch and each input set has one settled state. The 500 ms advance before each expect lets the lamps finish their thermal transients; the page states no timing.

Both pushbuttons up: 1Y-1X and 2Y-2X open, so neither coil path 1C-1E-1F / 2C-2E-2F carries current; relays 1 and 2 out, indicators dark; light 3 needs 1H-1G and 2H-2G both closed, neither is
script.quote: The following circuit and program represent the condition that if relay 1 is ON (=1) AND relay 2 is ON (=1) then light 3 will be ON (=1). Symbolically, A X B = C: ... Pushing pushbutton 1 causes relay 1 to close by providing current to the coil of relay 1. In a similar manner, pushbutton 2 controls the flow of current to the coil of relay 2. The normally open contacts of the two relays are used to effect the "AND" condition. Light 3 indicates when the "AND" condition is met—both relay 1 and relay 2 are closed (ON).
